source.title: Multi-attacks: Many images $+$ the same adversarial attack $\to$ many target labels

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains classifiers with real or randomly permuted CIFAR-10 labels and compares their susceptibility to multi-attacks, a new outcome not covered by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for fitting randomly assigned labels, but does not report its own training-error or test-error results for that finding. Its own random-label experiment measures multi-attack susceptibility.
record.test_reason: The study trains classifiers with random labels to compare adversarial multi-attack susceptibility. It reports no training accuracy, test accuracy, or classifier learning dynamics that test V1–V6; the statement about perfect random-label fitting is attributed to Zhang et al.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion for the random-label experiment: classifiers trained on randomly assigned labels are more susceptible to multi-attacks than classifiers trained on semantically meaningful labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares multi-attack susceptibility of classifiers trained on real versus randomly permuted labels; it does not reproduce the original random-label memorization measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: The random-label-trained ResNet50 permits more simultaneous attacks and is easier to attack at a given perturbation strength than the real-label comparator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training on random labels increases susceptibility to adversarial multi-attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.4 and Figure 6 report similar multi-attack susceptibility for real images and random-noise inputs to an existing classifier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-attacks can target real images and random-noise inputs with similar success.

record.code_released: GitHub (URL not stated in supplied text)
record.problems: The comparison is shown in Figure 7 without numeric values in the text; the text reports no uncertainty for this experiment.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error on random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative classifier training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Classifier training to zero error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across label corruption fractions.
Effects of explicit regularization and its removal on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise during classifier training.

record.verdict_notes: Neither adversarial optimization toward arbitrary target labels nor attacks on noise inputs measure classifier memorization of a randomly labeled training set.

versions.untested_parts: Whether the study's networks fit random labels to zero or near-zero training error, have chance test error, and do so without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence as the fraction of corrupted labels changes.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs to zero training error.
Training and test error across a sweep of random-label corruption fractions.
Effects of regularization, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal on fitting random labels and generalization.
Whether real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels during training.

rows.subject: ResNet50 trained on CIFAR-10 with real labels

rows.operation_detail: Optimized a multi-attack against the classifier for 500 steps using Adam at learning rate 10−2.
rows.measure: Number of images successfully attacked at once as a function of optimization step and perturbation strength.
rows.value: Figure 7 only; text says the random-label-trained models allow for more simultaneous attacks.
rows.note: Comparator for the randomly permuted-label model; the text does not give a numeric result for this model.
rows.check: This is a valid attack comparator, but its measure cannot establish any claim version.
